notes.title: Patch Update Version 1.21
notes.content:
[b]Patch Update Version 1.21[/b]
[i]Enhanced Precision and Immersion Update[/i]

What's New:
[list]
[*]   [b]Immersive Environments[/b]: Each surgery stage now features enhanced environments for a more immersive experience.
[*]   [b]Improved Physics[/b]: The peg transfer stages have received physics improvements, making the handling more realistic and responsive.
[*]   [b]Marathon Mode Fixes[/b]: Various bugs and issues in marathon mode have been addressed and fixed.
[*]   [b]Streamlined Game File Size[/b]: Optimizations have been made to reduce the overall game file size for a smoother installation and loading process.
[*]   [b]Hand Tracking Support[/b]: Added support for hand tracking using Quest 2 and 3 devices, optimized for use with a foot pedal.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Update Version 1.2
notes.content:
[b]Patch Update Version 1.2[/b]
[i]Enhanced Quality of Life and Visual Improvements
[/i]
What's New:
[list]
[*]  Vive Controller Integration: Support for Vive controllers now available (Note: Excludes Minimally Invasive demo level).
[*]  iKKEGOL Foot Pedal Support for clutch movements: For non-iKKEGOL brands, remap foot pedal inputs to "A" and "B" for seamless left and right pedal functionality.
[*]  Customizable Level Settings: Adjust stereoscopic screen, camera movement, and access the Reset view button from the levels.
[*]  Optimized Training Environment: The updated environment is now streamlined for better focus, utilizing fewer resources for a smoother experience.
[*]   Resolved an issue in the robot surgery demo where players were unable to remove screws.
[*]   Connect with Us: Social links now included in-game. Stay in touch and join our growing community on : [url=https://discord.gg/RAfsTSqnVG]Discord[/url].

The VR Vive support was a feature request from the community that we added for those that have the Vive but don't have Valve Index controllers. Due to the way the  flying works - it doesn't support the Vive controllers  that level is not available to Vive controller users in version 1.2.

The foot pedal clutch we recently introduced is an optional feature that enables surgeons to reposition the robot's arms while preserving the current orientation of the surgical instruments. This addition proves particularly beneficial during complex procedures where precise control of instruments is vital. Initially, our joystick button clutch was modeled after a commercial modular robot simulator, which did not incorporate foot pedals for clutch control. We are eager to receive feedback regarding your preferred setup and the reasons behind your choice.

[/list]
